hints: Ask yourself for each cell 1, 2 and 3: will this cell need to divide by mitosis many more times in the future, or is its dividing days over?
Remember telomeres shorten a little at every mitosis, so high telomerase is only useful in cells that must keep dividing, and transcription needs a nucleus with DNA.
walkthrough:
**Recall what telomerase is for**

Think of telomeres as protective caps on chromosomes. A little bit is lost at each mitosis.

Telomerase rebuilds them, so it is only worth making in cells that must go through many more mitotic cycles.

**Check cells 1 and 2**

Neutrophils are terminally differentiated phagocytes. They are short lived and do not divide further, so they do not need high telomerase.

Mature red blood cells in mammals have no nucleus and no DNA. With no genes to transcribe, they cannot transcribe telomerase at all.

**Check cell 3 and conclude**

Activated memory T-lymphocytes must divide very rapidly by mitosis during clonal expansion to make a large clone of effector cells. They need telomerase to protect telomeres through all those divisions.

So only 3 is correct, which matches option D.

options.A: Incorrect because neither 1 nor 2 needs high telomerase. Neutrophils do not divide further and mature red cells have no nucleus for transcription.
options.B: Incorrect because although 3 is correct, 1 is wrong. Neutrophils are short lived, non-dividing end cells.
options.C: Incorrect because 1 alone is wrong. Neutrophils will not go through many more mitotic cycles.
options.D: Correct because only 3 is right. Activated memory T-lymphocytes undergo rapid repeated mitosis in an immune response and need telomerase to maintain telomeres.
